newsitem.title: USA: Western Resources drops bid; Tyco, ADT complete deal.
newsitem.headline: Western Resources drops bid; Tyco, ADT complete deal.

text.p: Kansas utility Western Resources Inc. said Wednesday it was dropping its $3.5 billion hostile bid for ADT Ltd, clearing the way for completion of a friendly merger between ADT and Tyco International Ltd.
The Tyco deal, originally valued at $5.4 billion, joins the makers of fire and security alarms with markets in Europe and the United States.

Western, which owns 27 percent of ADT, said it will reap a $710 million gain on its conversion of ADT shares into Tyco stock. It said it will pursue a Bermuda court action against ADT that is related to the value of its ADT holdings.
The utility had been expected to drop the bid, which originally was valued at $22.50 per share. Last month, it cancelled a June 17 shareholders meeting on the proposed acquisition.
ADT disclosed in May that it was in talks with Western about dropping the bid, but Western had never confirmed those discussions.

Western launched its takeover effort in December after slowly amassing a big stake in Bermuda-based ADT. The bid was widely considered too low for a company that is a key player in the booming electronic security industry.
Western Resources stock closed down 32 cents at $32.5625 and ADT gained $2.50 to $36.25, both on the New York Stock Exchange. Tyco jumped $4.875 to end at $75.6875, also on the NYSE.
